name: PastePop – Clipboard History
description:
Windows-style Win+V clipboard history for GNOME. Press your shortcut and a small popup opens at the text cursor; pick an item and it is pasted into the app you were using.

* Text, images and copied files, with pins and search
* Emoji, symbols and kaomoji, typed straight into the app
* Skips passwords marked by password managers, apps you exclude, and everything while private mode is on

PastePop reads the clipboard to keep a history, stored only on this computer in ~/.local/share/pastepop. Nothing leaves your computer.

Choose a shortcut in the preferences, such as Super+V.
